<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx`  _(via sys_attachment (literal, a string literal in attach))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via assertReferencesResolve (symbol, a top-level function), sys_attachment (literal, a string literal in attach))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via sys_attachment (literal, a string literal in attach))_
- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via sys_attachment (literal, a string literal in attach))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via sys_attachment (literal, a string literal in attach))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via sys_attachment (literal, a string literal in attach))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **224** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **161** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **161**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **57** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **53** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 022b4e7eef42c54c3489175af3f3be870a994a9d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `63910be7a321423d219657e7246697df00b344e0` — the merge of head `b018a55affaa1c127d6b57cc5bc962aa9121e98e` into base `022b4e7eef42c54c3489175af3f3be870a994a9d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 63910be7a321423d219657e7246697df00b344e0 && git checkout 63910be7a321423d219657e7246697df00b344e0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 022b4e7eef42c54c3489175af3f3be870a994a9d b018a55affaa1c127d6b57cc5bc962aa9121e98e && git checkout -B drift-repro 022b4e7eef42c54c3489175af3f3be870a994a9d && git merge --no-ff b018a55affaa1c127d6b57cc5bc962aa9121e98e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 022b4e7eef42c54c3489175af3f3be870a994a9d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 022b4e7eef42c54c3489175af3f3be870a994a9d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b018a55affaa1c127d6b57cc5bc962aa9121e98e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: none + packages/core/src/security/vouched-reference.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-referential-integrity.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-attachment-service.ts, .changeset/sec-r16-attach-verb-vouched-file.md; read on `main` to judge them: packages/core/src/security/flow-write-reference-check.ts, packages/core/src/security/app-automation-elevation.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (insert path, `assertReferencesResolve` host), packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts (`referenceCheckContext`), packages/objectql/src/engine-transactions-section.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-scoped-context.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-hook-dispatch.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-compatibility-section.ts (`createContext`), packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts (`resolveRunDataContext`), packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-lifecycle.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts (`enforceFilesCapability`), packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-attachment.object.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs.

Reviewed at 2026-11-06T23:34Z. The PR is a security-seat order on a regression `main` carries since `eb96480dd6` (#31031); it has no card. Read: the PR body, its eight-file list, the three-dot diff against the merge base `b5106af62a`, the check-runs on the head, and the rule's code on `main`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

The change under review is one predicate flip and one call: `assertReferencesResolve` asks the caller's read door for a `lookup` / `master_detail` / `user` value unless `isVouchedReference(context, schema.name, field, value)` holds, and `FileAttachmentService.attach` sets the vouch on its caller-scoped `sys_attachment` insert for `(sys_attachment, file_id, fileId)` where `fileId` is the `randomUUID()` the same call wrote into `sys_file` in step ③. The system path (`attachFile`) sets no mark. Each judgment below is named right or wrong.

1. **No published door can carry, forge or widen the mark — right.** The key is `Symbol.for('objectstack.core.vouchedReferences')`. A JSON body, query string, header, stored row, flow definition or MCP argument spells string keys only; `ExecutionContextSchema.parse` keeps declared keys, and the one site that parses (`ObjectQL.createContext`, engine-compatibility-section.ts) carries only `APP_AUTOMATION_ELEVATION` across the parse, so this mark is dropped there, which is the right default; `structuredClone` drops symbol keys; a spread copies them, which is the design. The pin "a string key of the symbol's description is no mark" covers the one spelling a body could produce. The reader also refuses a non-object context, a non-string object or field, and a non-scalar id, so a crafted value in the `data` row cannot match a vouched entry by shape.

2. **The mark does not reach a flow the insert fires — right.** `resolveRunDataContext` (service-automation) builds a fresh object literal on both arms, system and user; it copies named fields off the trigger context and never spreads it. A record-change flow run under this insert therefore carries neither this mark nor sees the vouched id as admitted. The two marks `FLOW_WRITE_REFERENCE_CHECK` and this one never share a flow context.

3. **The mark does reach a hook's derived context under the insert — right as stated, and a residual the record names.** `ScopedContext.withRunAs('user')`, `sudo()` and the per-row hook contexts all spread the write's context (`{ ...this.executionContext, ... }`, `{ ...batchCtx, ... }`), so a hook's `ctx.api` write under the vouched insert carries the mark; the module header says so. What it admits is bounded: the same object, field and id only, and under `sudo()` / `runAs: 'system'` the context is `isSystem` without the flow mark, so the reference check is already exempt there and the vouch adds nothing. Every hook registered on `sys_attachment` on `main` is platform code (the three attach gates, the `enable.files` gate, the lifecycle hooks, the delete floor), and the lifecycle hooks write under `SYSTEM_CTX`, so no platform hook consumes the carried mark. The residual is an app-authored `runAs: 'user'` hook on `sys_attachment` writing a second `sys_attachment` row for the same file inside the same call; that row still meets the attach rule (parent EDIT as the caller), the `enable.files` gate and the file-reference gate, so it admits what the caller could do before #31031 for a file they own, and nothing more. Should-fix: make the vouch one-shot (consume it on the first admitted value, or strip it from the hook-derived context), with a pin; the mark's docblock then stops having to promise that hooks are harmless.

4. **The mark is scoped to the one insert — right.** The vouch is applied inline in the insert's `options.context` and nowhere else: `trxCtx` is built by `engine.transaction` as `{ ...base, transaction: trx }` before the vouch, the vouch spreads that object so the `transaction` property rides and the insert stays in the unit, and `store.updateFile` (the commit) runs under the metadata store's own system write context. The caller's own context object is not mutated (`vouchForReference` returns a fresh object). `requireUserContext` refuses a system context before the path is reached, so the mark never sits on an `isSystem` context from this writer. An insert sets off no cascade leg. The pin "after `attachFileAs`, the member's own insert naming the same file is refused" confirms nothing outlives the call.

5. **Keyed tightly enough — right.** `(object, field, id)` with `String()` on both sides; `schema.name` on the insert path is the canonical object name; `sys_attachment.file_id` is `Field.lookup('sys_file')` (platform-objects). A multi-valued field is judged per member and only the vouched member is admitted (pinned). Another id in the same field, the same id in another field, and the same id on another object are each refused (pinned). The reader accepts a numeric id and coerces it, exactly as the probe does.

6. **The existence probe is still tenant-kept — right.** The vouched branch calls `referenceExists(target, v, context)` with the caller's context; `referenceCheckContext` is `{ ...context, isSystem: true }`, so `tenantId` rides and a row in another organization is not found. The verb forces the file into the caller's organization: `request.organizationId` must equal the caller's `tenantId`, and a parent walled into another organization is refused as not found, so the probe finds exactly the row the call wrote. A vouched id that names no row is still refused (pinned).

7. **Other marks in the tree do not combine into a wider admit — right.** Core's security family holds two sibling marks: `FLOW_WRITE_REFERENCE_CHECK` (keeps the check ON for an elevated flow write; never co-occurs with this mark, see 2) and `APP_AUTOMATION_ELEVATION` (its only reader refuses). Neither reader consults this mark and this mark's reader consults neither. The driver, spec and metadata symbols found by census are brands on values or diagnostics, not context marks.

8. **Every other gate on the insert still judges the caller — right.** The context stays the caller's with `isSystem` absent: the CRUD middleware's object permission on `sys_attachment` (also asked up front by `assertMayAttach` through `explain`); the parent-EDIT attach rule and the `uploaded_by` stamp (`attachment-access-hooks` beforeInsert returns only on `ctx.session.isSystem`, stamps `ctx.session.userId` over whatever the client sent); `enable.files` (plugin-audit, judged on the parent object's definition, context-independent); the file-reference gate (returns only on `ctx.session.isSystem`, asks the download door's verdict as the caller — the uploader of the file is admitted by that door's own rule); RLS and FLS through the middleware chain on the caller's context; the owner stamp on `sys_file` (`owner_id: caller.userId`, step ③). The parent is read as the caller in step ②, and the parent reference on the row is judged through the caller's read door as before. The storage suite stands a middleware in for the permission layer; the dogfood pin runs the real `SecurityPlugin` with a member holding `sys_attachment` read/create and nothing on `sys_file`, and asserts `sys_file` stays unreadable to them after the print.

9. **The new public export from `@objectstack/core` — right to exist, and a posture change the record names.** The mark must live in a package both the setter (service-storage) and the reader (objectql) depend on; both already declare `@objectstack/core` (`workspace:*`) and already import from it, and core already hosts the two sibling marks, so the placement is the family's. The export is `VOUCHED_REFERENCES`, `vouchForReference`, `isVouchedReference` and the `VouchedReference` type, through `security/index.ts` and core's root `export *`. Two things follow. First, this is the first mark in that family whose reader ADMITS: the flow mark keeps a check on, the elevation mark only refuses, and app-automation-elevation.ts states that posture as a reason the family is safe. Second, the only thing confining `vouchForReference` to "a service verb, for a record the same call created" is prose in its docblock; any in-process plugin or service that imports core can call it. Should-fix: a call-site census gate (the repo's `check:` shape) that pins `vouchForReference` callers to an allowlist naming `file-attachment-service.ts`, so a second caller is a red gate and a review, not a grep someone remembers to run.

10. **The verb's premise holds — right.** The read-door rule judges a reference the caller chose; here the caller chose nothing: the id is minted in the call, the row is written for the caller, and the caller has already passed the verb's own authorization (`assertMayAttach` by the producer, and the insert's gates). The exemption is for one value whose provenance the writer itself established, which is the narrowest shape the three alternatives the body lists do not reach.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/sec-r16-attach-verb-vouched-file.md`: `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-storage` at `patch`. **Right** under ruling A: the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone, and `none` takes `patch`.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` — **right.** No key, value, type or default an author can write moves; the mark is in no schema.
- `Clause-②: no` — **defensible, not exact.** The clause asks whether the card widens a published accept set or public surface. No published door's accept set moves: every REST, MCP, flow and import write is judged exactly as before, the file the verb attached included (pinned), and the admit is reachable only in-process. But `@objectstack/core`'s root does gain three runtime names and a type, which is the public surface growing. The precedent is the sibling: #28881 added `FLOW_WRITE_REFERENCE_CHECK` and its two functions to the same index and declared `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with "nothing is widened". Should-fix: either re-declare `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and changeset, level unchanged under ruling A, or keep `no` and name that precedent in the body so the next reader does not re-derive this. Neither choice moves the level or the ADR-0087 disposition, so this is not a landing defect.
- The PR body and changeset carry both lines in the fixed spelling at line start.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **The browser attachments panel (the dev's open question).** The panel's two-step flow (presigned upload, then `POST /data/sys_attachment` through the generic data door) is refused for a member who holds the attach grant and nothing on `sys_file`; that refusal is #31031's, predates this PR, and this PR neither fixes nor worsens it. Of the three options: **A** (a server attach verb the panel calls, inheriting this vouch) does not fit this vouch's premise — the verb would not have created the file, so it would be vouching for a file the caller uploaded earlier, which is a different rule; **B** (judge `sys_attachment.file_id` by the storage file-reference gate instead of the read door) special-cases one object in the generic engine and is the shape the PR body rightly declined for the same reason; **C** (an owner-scoped read on `sys_file`, `owner_id` equals the caller) makes the read door answer truthfully for the row the caller already owns, keeps the generic rule whole, and needs no engine change — it is the fix whose premise matches the panel's. **Answer: C, as its own card.** Escalate the grant's shape to the maintainer (whether it ships as a default permission-set entry or an RLS rule on `sys_file`, and whether `enable.files` objects should imply it). **Leaving it out does not block this PR**: the PR's scope is the two server paths, and the panel path is a separate change with its own pins.
2. **Why `main` is green while the panel is refused.** `attachments-permission-matrix.dogfood.test.ts` runs on a fixture that grants `'*'` read, `sys_file` included, so no dogfood pin exercises a member with only the attach grant through the data door. The follow-up card above should carry such a pin; without it the panel fix has no gate.
3. **Checks on the head, as they stand at 2026-11-06T23:34Z.** 33 completed, none failed: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, every `Lint ·` job, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (aggregate), `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI` are `success`. 28 in progress: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1..8/8)`, `Test UI (1..16/16)`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · workspace`. The three `Dogfood Regression Gate (shard/3)` legs are `skipped` on this head, so the new dogfood pin (`print-service-archive.dogfood.test.ts`) ran only in the dev's local runs; the seat should wait for `Test Core` before landing and should know the dogfood shards did not exercise it here.
4. **The dev's audit of other service-internal caller-context writes.** Agrees with my own census of `sys_*` inserts and updates in `packages/services/*/src` and `packages/plugins/*/src` on `main`: share-link minting, approval approver rows, sharing projections, auth hooks and the storage metadata store write as the system; `admin-set-user-manager` writes under `authSystemWriteContext()` (system with attribution); the OAuth application update carries no context; `admin-user-endpoints`' grant write is admitted only to callers who read every user; flow CRUD nodes are a generic door by design. No second instance of this regression shape found.
5. **Design posture, for the record.** This is the first admitting mark in core's security family (see ① 9). It is acceptable because its admit is one value whose provenance the writer established in the same call, but the family's own docblocks should say the family now has one admitting member, and the census gate in ① 9 is what keeps it at one caller.

Must-fix: none.
Should-fix: ① 3 (one-shot vouch, with a pin); ① 9 (call-site census gate for `vouchForReference`); ② (re-declare `Clause-②: yes (widening)` or name the #28881 precedent); ③ 1 and 2 (the panel fix as its own card, option C, with a realistic-member dogfood pin).

Implemented-by: `claude/sec-hardening-r16`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibvynRbCtMndW8EHNGc`

**VERDICT: PASS**

队列构建 [42314301819](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42314301819) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Test Core (4/8)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42314301819/job/128223737092)** — 失败步骤: Run this shard's tests


> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
